name: Inositol
short: A safety review found only mild nausea, flatus and diarrhoea at the highest dose studied (12 g/day). In an uncontrolled 15-person pilot, an inositol blend did not disrupt lithium or valproate therapy.
text: A review of the clinical safety of myo-inositol found that only the highest dose studied (12 g/day) induced mild gastrointestinal side effects such as nausea, flatus and diarrhoea, and that the severity of side effects did not increase with the dosage; the authors noted that information on its safety remains scarce. In an uncontrolled pilot study of 15 adults taking lithium and/or valproic acid, a blend of myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol with alpha-lactalbumin was taken for 6 months with no changes or adjustments needed to their medicines and no recorded interference with the therapy; this was a small pilot study, and the authors described the possibility of inositol reducing the effectiveness of these medicines as a matter of concern.
